description: PROPOSAL -- awaiting sign-off. Disposition for every schema property with no column in the applied DDL (schema/schema.sql). Generated by applying the rules below in priority order; review and override per property as needed. Enforced by scripts/check_coverage.py.

dispositions.column: Add a real column to schema.sql. Requires a user_version bump.
dispositions.attribute: Persist via the generic `attributes` table. Must also be added to this table's `attribute_channel` in sql_codegen_map.json.
dispositions.rename: A column already exists under a different name. Add to this table's `renames` in sql_codegen_map.json; no DDL change.
dispositions.decomposed: The value is already stored, split across two or more existing columns. Needs a split/join rule in the mapper; no DDL change.
dispositions.skip: Does not persist. Must also be added to this table's `skip` in sql_codegen_map.json.
dispositions.covered-by-generic: Persisted generically in an existing JSON store (e.g. supplemental_attributes, type-discriminated); no dedicated table or column.

rules: 1. `dynamic_injector` -> skip. Links to a dynamics component; dynamics are not modeled in this schema.
2. A column already exists under a different name (e.g. R_th vs r_th) -> rename.
3. The value is already stored decomposed across existing columns (e.g. complex Y as y_g + y_b) -> decomposed.
4. References another entity -> column. A foreign key cannot be enforced inside a JSON attribute value, so a reference stored as an attribute is an invisible dangling pointer.
5. `available` -> column. Every query filters on it.

6. Present on fewer than half the mapped components -> attribute. A column would be mostly NULL. Generalises the existing hydro_generators attribute_channel (efficiency, active_power_limits_pump, turbine_type).

7. KEY -- identity or administrative/categorical (number, bustype, status, conformity, control_mode) -> column, AND indexed. Joins and filters in this schema run on ids, names, fuels and administrative fields.

8. DENSE PAYLOAD -- a physical parameter present on effectively every row -> column, NOT indexed. Justified by read cost, not queryability: demoting these to attributes adds ~149k rows (+46%) to the attributes table on cats_db_nodal.sqlite and turns a 10,825-row line scan into a ~65k-row join+pivot.
9. Everything else -> attribute. Sparse or peripheral device detail (converter tap settings, extinction angles, per-terminal parameters).
review_notes: Rule 7 covers identity, administrative, and categorical columns that queries actually join and filter on; rule 8 covers dense physical payload, which the schema almost never joins on. Only rule 7 carries an indexing obligation.

Sparse categoricals stay attributes rather than columns when an existing key already covers the same filter. loads.motor_technology, start_types, must_run, and power_mode all fall to entities.entity_type or rule 6 for this reason.

two_terminal_hvdc_lines merges the three PSY point-to-point HVDC variants (Generic, LCC, VSC) into one table. Only fields common to all three, such as reactive_power_limits_from/to, are columns; the roughly 60 variant-specific fields (converter control blocks, per-terminal limits and setpoints) are attributes. The four *_units discriminators are skipped because attributes.unit records each attribute row's own basis.

hydro_reservoirs.upstream_turbines, downstream_turbines, and upstream_reservoirs store entity-id arrays as attributes, even though JSON attributes give references no referential integrity. These likely need an association table like supplemental_attribute_associations; the fix is deferred to a separate decision.
loads carries 20 attribute dispositions, mostly the ZIP-model breakdown (constant/impedance/current x active/reactive x max), because each field is present on only 2 of the 7 merged load components.

sources.internal_voltage and sources.internal_angle are columns, not attributes, because they are the Thevenin phasor -- the component's core state, not optional metadata. Every other injector keeps its state as columns, and the schemas project these fields as columns too.
sources.base_voltage is a nullable column because a source's own base_voltage is not backfilled from balancing_topologies.base_voltage. Making it NOT NULL would force loaders to invent a value.

A variable-cost curve's unit depends on its curve form, so the operation_cost.<curve> conventions discriminate on JSON paths inside the same blob (value_curve.curve_type, plus variable_cost_type for a FuelCurve). INPUT_OUTPUT is a cost rate (USD/h), INCREMENTAL and AVERAGE_RATE are per-energy (USD/MWh), and a FuelCurve's curve is a heat rate (MMBtu/MWh).

The FUEL x INPUT_OUTPUT combination cannot be registered because SiennaSchemas Core/units.json has no fuel-rate (MMBtu/h) quantity type -- HeatRate only covers MMBtu/MWh. The generator refuses pairs absent from the vocabulary, so the row is omitted until a fuel-rate quantity is added upstream.

storage_units cost conventions register charge_variable_cost and discharge_variable_cost, not operation_cost.variable, because StorageCost has no such path. energy_shortage_cost and energy_surplus_cost remain unregistered.

thermal_generators, renewable_generators, and hydro_generators expose the variable cost curve as a queryable production_cost column, a GENERATED ALWAYS AS column deriving from operation_cost -- not a second copy of the data. A CHECK on operation_cost enforces a valid variable_cost_type and curve_type, wrapping json_extract in ifnull because a bare IN (...) would otherwise admit a missing curve as NULL. renewable_generators allows only COST curves, since RenewableGenerationCost has no registered unit for a FUEL curve.

storage_units keeps its cost curves inside operation_cost, unlike the generator tables which promote them to a dedicated column. This is deliberate: operation_cost there is the StorageCost object as the schemas define it, and its curves are already registered and power_units-guarded in place.

attributes.magnitude and attributes.voltage_limits carry their own unit/quantity_type inline instead of using unit_conventions.base_power_ref/base_voltage_ref, because an attributes row's owner is polymorphic (entity_id -> entities) and has no single fixed base-lookup path.

Upstream added a required per-row base_power to AreaInterchange, all three two-terminal HVDC variants, and FACTSControlDevice, matching the per-row base_power GridDB already stores on transmission_lines, discrete_controlled_ac_branches, sources, and tmodel_hvdc_lines; these are dispositioned column but not yet implemented. TModelHVDCLine instead carries a required base_current (A) and no base_power; GridDB now stores base_current on tmodel_hvdc_lines, the one sanctioned exception to the per-row base_power rule.

The schema's *_units discriminator properties map onto the DB's parameter_units column by rename where the vocabularies align (ImpedanceUnitBasis and VoltageUnitBasis both mean COMPONENT_BASE/NATURAL_UNITS). fixed_admittance and switched_admittance instead carry admittance_units as their own column. two/three-winding admittance_units and two_terminal_hvdc_lines.setpoint_voltage_units are skipped because the fields they'd discriminate live in the attributes channel, where attributes.unit records the basis per row.
DataSource and GeographicInfo supplemental attributes are stored generically in supplemental_attributes JSON, discriminated by TYPE, with no dedicated columns -- dispositioned covered-by-generic.

TwoTerminalVSCLine's rated_ac_voltage_from/to join rated_dc_voltage as kV attribute-name conventions. Its basis-dependent fields (voltage_limits_from/to, dc_voltage_droop_from/to) stay unregistered because a convention's discriminator_column names a sibling column that an attributes row does not have; each stored row instead carries its own unit/quantity_type, validated by the insert trigger.
